main_diagnosis: The simulator achieves a high neg_avg_log_marginal_NLE of 25.4, indicating substantial mismatch in spike statistics. The primary structural gap is that the X2 channel slot (params[8], params[9]) is completely unused, leaving only INaP (X1) to supplement the base HH model. With just one additional channel, the model cannot independently control both spike rate and ISI regularity simultaneously — INaP shifts the effective threshold (affecting spike count), but provides no mechanism to regulate the inter-spike interval spacing or AHP recovery kinetics. A slow voltage-gated K+ current (M-current / Kv7) in the X2 slot would provide orthogonal control over ISI regularity, directly improving the spike count, voltage variance, skewness, and kurtosis summary statistics that drive NLE.

issues.description: The X2 channel slot is intentionally left empty, but at NLE=25.4 the parsimony argument is not supported by the evidence. The M-current (I_M / Kv7) is the ideal X2 candidate: it is a slow, non-inactivating, voltage-activated K+ current that activates near rest (-60 to -40 mV) with time constants of 10–50 ms. Crucially, at small conductances it regularises ISI spacing without causing adaptation to silence or burst firing — exactly matching the target tonic spiking description. Unlike Ih (which was correctly removed for causing tonic depolarisation), I_M is hyperpolarising and stabilises the resting potential. Formulation: I_M = gbar_M * w_inf(V) * (V - E_K), where w_inf(V) = 1/(1+exp(-(V-V_half_M)/10)) with tau_w ~ 20 ms (first-order ODE), gbar_M = params[8] (∈ [1e-4, 5] mS/cm²), V_half_M = -params[9] (params[9] ∈ [1e-4, 150] → V_half ∈ [-150,0] mV, posterior expected ~-50 to -35 mV). This gives independent posterior axes for spike count (via INaP V_half/gbar) and ISI regularity (via I_M gbar/V_half), resolving the current single-channel degeneracy.
issues.location: forward() — channel slot X2, params[8] and params[9] currently unused
issues.suggestion: Implement I_M using params[8] (gbar_M) and params[9] (V_half_M). Add a new state variable w (M-current activation gate), initialise w[:,0] = w_inf(V[:,0]), integrate with exact exponential update using fixed tau_w=20ms. Add current term: I_M = gbar_M * w * (V - E_K). Add to tau_V_inv: +gbar_M * w[:, i-1] / C. Add to V_inf numerator: +gbar_M * w[:, i-1] * E_K. This gives the inference two independent inferred conductances with complementary effects on spike statistics.

issues.description: The INaP Boltzmann parameterisation V_half_NaP = -params[7] with params[7] ∈ [1e-4, 150] produces a V_half prior over [-150, ~0] mV. The physiological range for cortical INaP is -65 to -40 mV, which occupies only ~17% of the prior support. With NLE=25.4 still high after several iterations, the wide prior likely causes the posterior sampler to waste capacity exploring non-physiological V_half values near -150 mV (full INaP inactivation) or near 0 mV (excessive persistent Na+ causing runaway depolarisation and pathological spike counts). Additionally, there is no upper clip on gbar_NaP; values >3 mS/cm² risk creating a sodium window current large enough to prevent proper repolarisation, producing plateau potentials rather than tonic spiking.
issues.location: forward() — params[7] (V_half_NaP) and params[6] (gbar_NaP) prior range interpretation
issues.suggestion: Tighten the effective range by re-parameterising: use V_half_NaP = -params[7] * 0.5 so the prior maps to [-75, 0] mV (centred on the physiological range), or add a soft sigmoid clamp: V_half_NaP = -30.0 - 40.0 * torch.sigmoid(params[7] - 75.0) to constrain to [-70, -30] mV without hard bounds. For gbar_NaP, add a soft clip: gbar_NaP = torch.clamp(params[:, 6], 0.0001, 3.0) to prevent runaway persistent Na+ current.
